validity.researcher_notes: Building on the cancelled-review leg already staged for this row (batches/india-gas/staging/cancelled-review/rows/P0451.json), which independently confirmed Status=cancelled/CancelledYear=2009 and the full route/length/cost chain with high-tier sourcing — not re-deriving any of that. That leg's own Length fill quotes gulfoilandgas.com's project timeline verbatim breaking the planned 2,700 km route into three legs: '1100 km in Iran and 1000 km to Pakistan and in case of agreement with India it will continue 600 km in Indian Territory' (1100+1000+600=2700, internally consistent) — i.e. the India-side 600 km was explicitly CONTINGENT on an agreement that never materialized. India formally withdrew in 2009 (two independent sources, offshore-technology.com and dawn.com, both already verified by the cancelled-review leg) before construction or detailed routing on the Indian leg ever began; Iran and Pakistan then proceeded bilaterally without India. Given that, a drawn route whose last endpoint lands in Pakistan near Karachi (24.916, 67.039) — Karachi being one of the two named Pakistani transit cities in the same source ('Pakistan's major cities of Karachi and Multan') — is exactly the outcome you'd expect from a route drawn to the extent the corridor was ever concretely planned/pursued (the Iran-Pakistan ~2,100 km), stopping where the cancelled, never-detailed 600 km Indian extension would have begun. This is the endpoint_country flag's 'correctly-drawn partial route' case the brief specifically calls out, not a start/end-country data error. I am not proposing any new coordinates to extend the route into India, per the standing rule against fabricating geometry for a segment that was cancelled before it was ever routed.
